title: Qantas Sets Mid-2028 for First Nonstop Sydney–New York Flights
excerpt: The 18-hour Project Sunrise service, on sale from August 2027, will be the first commercial nonstop link between Australia and New York.
body:
• Qantas will launch nonstop Sydney–New York flights in mid-2028, the second confirmed Project Sunrise route after Sydney–London.
  • The roughly 18-hour flight cuts more than three hours off current one-stop journeys; tickets go on sale in August 2027.
  • Specially configured Airbus A350-1000ULR jets with extra fuel tanks will fly the route, each carrying 238 passengers across four cabins.

Qantas has put a date on one of commercial aviation's longest-held ambitions: nonstop flights between Sydney and New York will begin in mid-2028, the airline announced Tuesday at a reception in New York. The service, part of the carrier's Project Sunrise ultra-long-haul program, will be the first nonstop commercial link between Australia and New York. Tickets go on sale in August 2027.

The flight will take about 18 hours — more than three hours faster than today's one-stop services via Auckland, Los Angeles or Dallas-Fort Worth, according to the airline.

The aircraft making it possible

The route will be flown by specially configured Airbus A350-1000ULR aircraft fitted with an additional 20,000-litre fuel tank, giving them a range of more than 16,000 kilometres and endurance of up to 22 hours airborne. Qantas has ordered 12 of the jets, each configured with 238 seats across four cabins, including six first-class suites and 52 business-class suites.

The first test aircraft is in the final stages of its flight-test program and recently completed a 24-hour, 24-minute nonstop flight from Melbourne to Toulouse — which Qantas says is the longest flight by a commercial airliner to date. The first aircraft is due for delivery in April 2027. Qantas pilots are already training on Australia's first A350 simulator in Sydney, with more than 360 pilots and 1,200 cabin crew expected to be trained before the fleet is complete.

Why New York, why now

New York is the second Project Sunrise route to be confirmed, following Sydney–London nonstop flights that begin in October 2027. Qantas says demand between Australia and the United States keeps climbing: visitor arrivals from the US are up 5 percent year-on-year, and the airline's own New York traffic has nearly doubled since 2023.

"Demand in and out of New York on Qantas has nearly doubled since 2023 and the appetite for non-stop, ultra long-haul flying has also continued to grow, with intent to book rising from 58 to 70 per cent since February this year, and reaching 80 per cent among premium travellers," the airline said.

"Conquering the tyranny of distance has been part of who Qantas is from the very beginning. Reaching New York non-stop completes a vision we set out many years ago."

— Vanessa Hudson, CEO, Qantas Group

The mid-2028 timeline marks a shift from Hudson's earlier suggestion that New York could start in late 2027 at less-than-daily frequency before scaling up as more aircraft arrive.

A decades-long ambition

Project Sunrise was first announced by then-CEO Alan Joyce in 2017, and the New York route has been its signature prize ever since. Qantas first flew to New York in 1958 — via Fiji, Honolulu and San Francisco — as part of its inaugural round-the-world service. Today it operates a daily one-stop Sydney–New York service via Auckland. The airline projects the ultra-long-haul flights will add $400 million to earnings over five years and lift profit margins from 4 to 10 percent.

What it means for diaspora travelers

Australia is home to one of the world's fastest-growing Indian communities, and a large share of Australia–US travel already moves through the hubs Qantas is bypassing. A faster Sydney–New York link adds capacity on a corridor many Indian Australians use for business and family travel to North America. More broadly, the A350-1000ULR economics Qantas is proving out are the same ones that could one day make ultra-long-haul nonstops viable on other diaspora-heavy corridors.

What's next

Tickets open in August 2027. Watch for pricing — ultra-long-haul premium cabins are where Qantas expects the real returns — and for whether the airline confirms a third Project Sunrise destination once the first aircraft are delivered.
